title: Broker Performance dashboard (API + UI)
objective: Brokers dashboard per spec FR-57 / PRD 15.1: six KPIs, Top Brokers ranking, quadrant scatter matrix, and the full ranked broker table with loss patterns.
scope: Quadrant palette shared with RM Performance (single source)
implementation_details: Features/Dashboards/BrokerPerformance/GetBrokerPerformanceQuery: KPIs — ActiveBrokers (brokers with activity in period), BrokerQuotes, BrokerConversion, WonViaBrokers, AvgTurnaround (down=good), OverdueFollowUps; TopBrokers: ranking by quote volume with count + conversion% columns; BrokerMatrix: per broker {x: quoteVolume, y: conversionRate, size: wonPremium, quadrant} — quadrant classification by median (or configured) volume/conversion split into the four PRD 15.3 categories; BrokerTable: all partners ranked by volume with columns broker(+primary contact), tier chip, branch, quotes, conversion (green strong/red weak), won premium, avg TAT, overdue count, top loss reason (mode of lost reasons on broker's lost items)

features/dashboards/BrokerPerformancePage.tsx: KPI row, TopBrokersRanking (horizontal bars), BrokerMatrixScatter (Recharts scatter with bubble size + quadrant background shading and legend from shared quadrantPalette constant), BrokerPerformanceTable full-width
Broker rows drill to filtered lead/quote lists via useDrill

T-043 amendment (docs/ui-remediation/plan.md, AC-082): build every screen part of this task on the shared design-system layer from T-043 — src/ui/src/theme/components.css classes (.qiq-card, .qiq-btn, .qiq-chip, .qiq-table-wrap, .qiq-kpi-*, .qiq-menu) and components/common/Icon.tsx — never ad-hoc inline styling or new CSS files. Before marking IMPLEMENTED, do a side-by-side check against docs/prototype/screenshots/QuoteIQ - Brokers.png at ~1670px: layout regions, card composition, chart types, chip/color semantics must match the prototype (subject to the PRD's documented deviations for this screen, e.g. lead-vs-quote labeling, excluded prototype-only widgets). Record the comparison result in this task's history.

e2e: dashboard-brokers.spec.ts: widgets render with seeded brokers; matrix quadrant colors match legend; table conversion coloring; broker row drill-through

findings.summary: Broker-performance permission gate: two candidate permissions exist (Dashboards.ViewBrokerPerformance vs the reserved Brokers.ViewPerformance). Gated on dashboards.view_broker_performance.
findings.detail: PermissionCatalog carries both Dashboards.ViewBrokerPerformance ('dashboards.view_broker_performance') and a reserved Brokers.ViewPerformance ('brokers.view_performance', commented 'reserved for T-034, not yet wired'). Chose Dashboards.ViewBrokerPerformance for consistency with the executive/pipeline endpoints AND because the seeded Executive Viewer role (SeedUsers.cs) is granted ONLY dashboards.view_broker_performance (not brokers.view_performance) — gating on the latter would 403 that role. The reserved Brokers.ViewPerformance is now a redundant/legacy catalog entry no endpoint references; flagged for a human to either remove it or repurpose it (not touched by this task).

findings.summary: Matrix quadrant split rule: median vs configured. Used MEDIAN of active brokers' quote volume and (non-null) conversion as the axis split.
findings.detail: PRD 15.3 does not define a configurable split threshold and no tenant-settings field exists for one, so the default split rule is the median of the plotted brokers' quote volume and of their non-null conversion rates (QuadrantClassifier.Median). The payload carries the resolved VolumeSplit/ConversionSplit so a future configured-split variant is a drop-in. Classification runs SERVER-SIDE (payload carries each broker's quadrant) via the shared Domain.Metrics.QuadrantClassifier, which the RM matrix (T-035) reuses. Flagged for confirmation that median (not a configured threshold) is the intended default.

findings.summary: Table conversion green-strong/red-weak threshold and null KPI deltas are documented decisions pending spec confirmation.
findings.detail: (a) PRD 15.1 says table conversion renders 'green when strong, red when weak' without an absolute cutoff; the table colors green at/above the matrix median conversion split and red below it (data-relative, consistent with the quadrant classification) rather than an arbitrary absolute %. (b) Broker KPI cards carry null period-over-period deltas (the prototype shows deltas like '+11% vs Apr 1-30'): brokers have no reliable prior-period baseline in the current data and no delta was hand-computable deterministically, so deltas are null — matching the Pipeline dashboard's precedent of null deltas where a prior comparable window is not derived. (c) Quadrant low/low renders in the neutral token (--qiq-quadrant-low-low = neutral gray) whereas the prototype colors bottom-left brokers red; this honors the pre-existing T-031 documented token decision (tokens.css) to reserve red/danger for at-risk semantics and use one consistent palette. All three are surfaced for human review, not silently resolved.

findings.summary: Ruling on F-034-1 (permission gate): ACCEPTED, non-blocking. Gate choice verified correct with no seeded-role regression.
findings.detail: Verified DashboardEndpoints.cs line 34 gates GET /broker-performance on PermissionCatalog.Dashboards.ViewBrokerPerformance ('dashboards.view_broker_performance'). Confirmed the seeded Executive Viewer role (SeedUsers.cs line 89) is granted ViewBrokerPerformance, so it reaches the endpoint (no T-044 regression); the 403 gate test passes. The reserved Brokers.ViewPerformance ('brokers.view_performance', PermissionCatalog.cs line 152/285) is now an orphaned catalog entry referenced by no endpoint (still granted to Sales Head at SeedUsers.cs line 64 harmlessly). Non-blocking CLEANUP NOTE for a human: remove or repurpose Brokers.ViewPerformance; not required for T-034 PASS.

findings.summary: Ruling on F-034-2 (median split) and F-034-3 (median-relative table coloring / null KPI deltas / low-low neutral token): all ACCEPTED, non-blocking.
findings.detail: F-034-2: median axis split is a defensible default — PRD 15.3 defines no configurable threshold, and BrokerMatrixDto carries VolumeSplit/ConversionSplit so a configured variant is a drop-in; classification runs server-side via the shared Domain QuadrantClassifier (verified). F-034-3(a): table green-strong/red-weak keyed to the matrix conversion median split is consistent with the quadrant classification and honours 'green when strong, red when weak' with no absolute cutoff in the PRD. F-034-3(b): null broker KPI deltas match the Pipeline precedent (no reliable prior-period baseline in current data). F-034-3(c): low/low renders the neutral --qiq-quadrant-low-low token (tokens.css lines 76/133 = --qiq-neutral) instead of prototype red, honouring the pre-existing T-031 palette decision to reserve danger for at-risk semantics. All three are documented, sensible defaults surfaced for human review, none block PASS.

findings.summary: quadrantPalette single-source is clean and reusable, but the T-031 stopgap it claims to resolve still exists in parallel (duplicate quadrant palette in palettes.ts + dead ScatterChartWidget).
findings.detail: quadrantPalette.ts IS a clean, broker-agnostic single source (generic PRD 15.3 labels, keyed to the server payload quadrant, --qiq-* tokens only) driving BOTH the BrokerMatrixScatter ReferenceArea shading AND the legend, and is genuinely reusable by T-035 unchanged — the reusability contract holds. HOWEVER, src/ui/src/components/dashboards/palettes.ts still exports a second, parallel QUADRANT_PALETTE + MatrixQuadrant type + resolveMatrixQuadrant, and src/ui/src/components/dashboards/charts/ScatterChartWidget.tsx still consumes them while being referenced only by rechartsWidgets.test.tsx (no live dashboard). So the T-031 stopgap this task's history claims to 'resolve' actually remains as a duplicate. Colors CANNOT diverge because both map to the same --qiq-quadrant-* tokens in tokens.css, so this is non-blocking; but T-035 must consolidate (delete the palettes.ts quadrant trio + dead ScatterChartWidget, or re-export them from quadrantPalette.ts) to avoid accidentally reusing the wrong source. Recommend addressing in T-035.

findings.summary: Minor integration-test coverage gaps (non-blocking): avg-turnaround numeric value, overdue-follow-ups KPI value, and per-scope broker drill are not asserted.
findings.detail: The five Api.Tests broker cases strongly cover ranking-by-volume + conversion, TopLossReason mode, matrix bubble=wonPremium + median splits + PRD 15.3 quadrant assignment, filter narrowing, and the 403 gate against a hand-computed fixture (all passing). Not asserted: the avg_turnaround KPI is checked only for GoodDirection (not its numeric value), the overdue_follow_ups KPI value is not asserted though the fixture seeds one overdue Beta lead, and the registered broker drill scopes (Won/Lost/OverdueFollowUps) are not each exercised end-to-end at the API level. QuadrantClassifierTests already covers the boundary/median/null-conversion cases. These are optional hardening, not blockers.
